notes.title: The Wind and the Wilting Blossom Review
notes.content:
The Wind and the Wilting Blossom is a bit of a strange one for wargamers, but getting past its roguelike overworld and RPG elements one finds an intriguing tactical game where planning around enemy moves is as important as positioning and the correct application of force.

Set in an alternate history Heian Japan, one in which Oya Taro Mitsukuni failed to put down the Heiji rebellion and instead unleashed a horde of Yokai, led by the witch daughter of Taira no Masakado herself, Takiyasha. She now seeks to consume all of Japan in the fires of hell for their affront to her family. A tale as old as time.

In practice it means players take on the role of Oya Taro Mitsukuni himself or a variety of unlockable heroes and legends of the period, including my personal favourite Murasaki Shikibu, author of The Tale of Genji, as they gather an army while fleeing the tidal wave of darkness pursuing them.

Gameplay is split between an overworld RPG, in which a player's hero and their warband navigate through a ravaged Japan, encountering story elements that require decisions, recruit and equip their forces, and engage in tactical battles against Yokai and other undesirables like bandits.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: Release Devblog
notes.content:
When we started working 4ish years ago on a little game about Japanese mythology and a period in Japanese history that's often unexplored, we had no idea what to expect in terms of players, support, and response. As of this writing, we’ve tracked nearly 2000 runs in 1.0! Through Early Access and now into Full Release, your bug hunting, feedback, and kind words have made this small, part-time team incredibly happy.

The story of The Wind and Wilting Blossom is far from over - we have a slew of content updates planned for the coming months. It’s worth nothing that we may juggle a few of these items around based on feedback, but broadly speaking, this is what’s next.

First things first - we have a small update coming in the next week focused primarily on tackling a couple of launch day bugs, but let’s get to the fun stuff:

[b]1.1 Yokai, Yokai, Yokai[/b]
Our first major update will feature new yokai enemies, mostly in the early game. More variety early is critical, since the starting regions are what players see most frequently. We'll also implement a Bestiary that provides information on encountered enemies, their abilities, and a bit of lore.

[b]1.2 The Bones[/b]
There is a certain boney beast whose absence looms large in the current endgame. He’ll be coming in this update to terrorize the party. We also have a healthy backlog of new Events to implement, and we’ll include 25+ here.

[b]1.3 Party Time[/b]
The third major update will add two Allies and a new Leader (with, of course, three distinct layouts).

[b]1.4 Bosses[/b]
We're in the very early stages of a boss system overhaul to accommodate multiple, randomized bosses at each Boss Story location. This will necessitate some light story changes to provide hints on which Boss to plan for in a particular Region.

We'll continue to sprinkle in some new Events with each update, and we have at least a half dozen new Weapons planned as well - with a focus on providing more variety among Ammo and Support types. Of course, you can also expect more achievements, bug fixes, balance tweaks, and quality of life improvements through each of the updates.

Thanks again for your support and encouragement.

- Picklefeet Games

notes.title: The Wind and Wilting Blossom is available NOW
notes.content:
We get it - you probably want to play the game rather than read our blather, but we'd be fools not to make a quick launch announcement.

We launched to Early Access at the end of April, and projected about six months to get out of EA. It (clearly) took us a little bit longer than we'd planned, but we believe the extra time and love was worth it. The game feels worlds more polished than the EA launch, and we've added so much new content that we're really excited about.

We'd be remiss not to briefly mention the folks and organizations that have advocated for us during (and often before!) EA:
[list]
[*]All of our EA purchasers and players (particularly those of you that playtested even earlier)
[*]Our Discord and Twitter communities
[*]The streamers and journalists willing to cover an EA game from a tiny studio no one's ever heard of
[*]Seattle Indies Expo for being the only convention that gave us any time or floor space
[/list]

Now go get back to the game! If you're enjoying it, it would mean the world to us if you'd take a few minutes to write a positive Steam review, tell your friends about it, and join us on Twitter or Discord. There's more stuff to come (we're particularly enamored with an annoying enemy who will steal your wado), so stay tuned.

- Picklefeet Games

notes.title: June Devblog
notes.content:
[b]Hello![/b]

Before we get into it, let us take a moment to thank you all for your support, bug submissions, and feedback up to this point. It has all been tremendously helpful in guiding our prioritization as we’ve released updates. Please continue to keep us honest and engaged via Discord and Twitter.

One of the consistent themes in feedback to date has been the idea that success in the game feels too random at times. We agree, and that's the primary focus of this blog and of the next update. We’ll have a host of other goodies in addition to a balance overhaul, which will make this our largest update so far. Thus, it will take a bit more time than some of the previous updates, but we are confident it will be worth the effort.

[b]Tiering, Progression, and the Fight Against Complete Randomnes[/b]s

In the next update, Allies, Weapons, and Charms will all have “Tiers” associated with them. As you might expect, more powerful Tiers will unlock as you progress through the regions of the game. Within each tier is a common/uncommon/rare hierarchy - the higher the rarity, the more powerful the unit or item will be. By converting all of our party elements into this rarity/tier system, we are able to break everything down into smaller chunks and introduce things gradually across regions, facilitating a better and more natural feeling progression.

In order to support this improvement (and for other reasons we'll mention in the next section), we needed to rebalance almost everything in the game. For the past few weeks we've been re-running much of the math to make sure each element of the game is appropriately balanced. In the past, many of our Weapons and Allies have been somewhat flat in terms of their relative power within their respective type. 

When this update launches, you will notice a change in many elements of the game - almost everything has been made more powerful, and Allies have been reconfigured to make levelling up more impactful and important. As a result, enemies also received their own rebalance to match these player-side changes. So expect to hate certain enemies even more than before!

You’ll still get the feeling of some good or bad luck occasionally, but having a run of “bad luck” will feel less impactful now. The goal is to make the feeling of randomness far less swingy.

Today, because all elements are available at the start of the game, there is less reason to invest in weaker units, and the metagame revolves around the hunt for specific Allies and Weapons. Because enemies are balanced against those better Allies, the game can feel extremely challenging at times without the “best” allies. Unfortunately for most of you, these coming balance changes mean you may finally need to invest some scrolls in improving those Farmers :).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35640594/024230ab35cfd2d9a7dd069c8a99a0066e3299ca.png[/img]

[b]Two New Regions![/b]

Part of the reason we need this rebalancing is because the time has arrived to expand the game world. With the next update, we’ll be adding regions for Tohoku and Hokkaido (known as Ezogashima during the Heian period, and thus, in the game as well). On launch, these regions will be similar to the existing regions of the game, but we have more planned for Ezogashima that will arrive in future releases. For example, events that are unique to the island that cannot be encountered anywhere else in the game world.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35640594/678ee9b602bd532215fd37c256ee7202d76d000c.png[/img]

[b]An Explosive Yokai[/b]

We're also introducing another yokai to frustrate you, the Katawaguruma. This yokai will explode in a fiery mess, setting your party and the surrounding terrain ablaze with the new Burning status effect (Armor and then HP damage every turn until Cured).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35640594/685b8e92e7ad103ef68408093cdaa88db7f1b4c0.png[/img]

[b]A New Boss[/b]

This update will also include a new Boss with an icy disposition.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35640594/eee5fa7498253638d10e71c12adea9e25341bc19.png[/img]

[b]More Charms[/b]

We are adding a host of new Charms with corresponding Achievements. Many of these charms are themed around defense, like granting party Immunity to certain Status Effects or weather events. We are also introducing a few Charms focused on amplifying specific Allies, to encourage more variation in party builds.

[b]Rebalanced Economy[/b]

We are rebalancing the Resource economy. You'll see far more XP scrolls than before with a much better feeling of progression.


Thanks again for your support and feedback. We look forward to sharing this update with you soon!

- Picklefeet Games

notes.title: Update 0.6.11
notes.content:
Update 0.6.11 is now live!
[list]
[*] Added an additional Lightning strike to stormy battles
[*] Increased the damage of Lightning strikes to 2 from 1
[*] Added an additional Lightning strike to make them harder to ignore
[*] Improved the "darkness wave" to start at the correct time and to start from a more optimal location depending on region
[*] Reduced rewards from the "darkness wave" battles
[*] Introduced a scaling system to make each subsequent "darkness wave" battle in one region harder
[*] Reduced the Armor and HP of the much hated Kijo yokai
[*] Changed the difficulty scaling of the Kijo yokai to make her more likely to appear in later regions although she still may make a rare early appearance to ruin your hopes and dreams
[*] Increased the Armor and HP of the Nure Onna yokai but reduced its Damage
[*] Added a Credits menu to the Main Menu

Fixes
[*] Fixed an issue where users with a touchscreen monitor could not use their mouse
[*] Fixed a crash caused by a Treasure Chest trap
[*] Fixed a crash caused by multiple triggers of the End Turn button
[*] Fixed a crash caused by a unit dying while afflicted with multiple Status Effects
[*] Fixed an issue where Fleeing during weather battles caused the game to hang
[*] Fixed an issue where any source of non-Attack damage (Bleed, Traps, Weather, etc.) added extra damage if a unit was afflicted with Vulnerable
[*] Fixed an issue where if you moused over a Leader, Layout, or other Tooltip in the Leader Select menu or Achievements menu and hit escape the tooltip would get stuck to your cursor
[/list]

notes.title: Update 0.6.10
notes.content:
- Implemented a brand new main menu
- Allies purchased in shops will now play the correct sound
- Fixed an issue where the mouseover tooltip on Allies in shops would get stuck on-screen

notes.title: Update 0.6.9
notes.content:
- Shinto Priest Ally art was updated to shorten the arms a bit
- Added Character Level to bottom-left Leader and Ally portraits in combat
- Added clarification to Jubokko tree ability to indicate that they do not move
- Jubokko monster's attack and heal range increased to 2 from 1 to make them more threatening
- Onikuma's retaliate ability will no longer fire if the onikuma is knocked back out of range of the knocker
- Onikuma's retaliate ability now deals 2 damage to match his normal attack damage
- Added a Move icon and Move value to the bottom-right monster portraits in combat
- Naigama, Bo, Nodachi, and Naginata Weapons had their damage increased to 2 from 1 to make them more useful
- Fixed a bug where you had enough Wado to Heal All in a shop but the button was greyed out
- Added missing Weapon name headers to Weapons in the Achievement window
- Shinto Priests will no longer betray the party by curing enemy units in combat
- Fixed a few event typos
